steps.tx: The commonest bladder cancer arising from the inner lining is **transitional cell carcinoma**. It lines the whole urinary tract, so tumours can appear in bladder, ureter and kidney pelvis. Smoking is the strongest risk factor. It accounts for roughly nine of ten bladder cancers, and quitting smoking lowers the risk only slowly over many years.
steps.say: Transitional cell carcinoma lines the whole urinary tract, and smoking remains its strongest risk factor.

vis.caption: Bladder tumour seen through a cystoscope. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Visible blood in urine without any pain is **painless haematuria**. It is the presenting feature in most bladder cancers and always needs investigation. Even one episode in an older adult should not be dismissed. Cystoscopy, direct telescope inspection of the bladder, is mandatory even when a urine infection is found, because infection and tumour can coexist.
steps.say: Painless visible blood in urine presents most bladder cancers and always needs investigation, even once.

steps.tx: Workers exposed to industrial dyes and rubber chemicals face risk from **aromatic amines**. These substances concentrate in urine and damage the bladder lining over years. Long latency means cancers appear decades after exposure. The classic culprits are 2-naphthylamine and benzidine, so a full occupational history belongs in every haematuria assessment.
steps.say: Aromatic amines from dye and rubber work concentrate in urine and cause bladder cancer decades later.

steps.tx: Chronic infection with the water snail parasite causes **Schistosoma haematobium** bladder disease. Years of inflammation drive the lining toward squamous cancer rather than the usual type. It remains important in parts of Africa and the Middle East. Its eggs lodge in the bladder wall, and praziquantel kills the parasite but cannot reverse cancer change that has already developed.
steps.say: Schistosoma haematobium causes chronic bladder inflammation that drives squamous cancer in endemic regions.

steps.tx: A bladder cancer made of flat keratin producing cells is **squamous carcinoma bladder**. It follows chronic irritation from stones, catheters or parasites. It tends to be muscle invasive when found. Unlike the usual type, it responds poorly to bladder preserving treatment, so removal of the whole bladder is usually advised.
steps.say: Squamous carcinoma of the bladder follows chronic irritation and tends to invade muscle when found.

steps.tx: Endoscopic removal of a bladder tumour through the urethra is **TURBT**. Transurethral resection of bladder tumour both diagnoses and stages the disease. Muscle in the specimen tells whether invasion has occurred. A specimen without detrusor muscle, the bladder wall muscle, is inadequate for staging, and repeat resection is needed when muscle is absent.
steps.say: Transurethral resection removes bladder tumours for diagnosis and staging, with muscle showing invasion depth.

steps.tx: Live tuberculosis vaccine washed into the bladder to prevent recurrence is **intravesical BCG**. It provokes a local immune attack on tumour cells after resection of high risk surface tumours. Flu like symptoms and bladder irritation are common effects. Treatment is usually weekly bladder washes for six weeks, and it is withheld during bleeding or urine infection because BCG can enter the blood.
steps.say: Intravesical BCG provokes a local immune attack after resection of high risk surface bladder tumours.

steps.tx: Tumours limited to the lining without muscle invasion are called **non muscle invasive** cancers. They recur often but progress less frequently. Regular cystoscopic surveillance catches recurrence early. Roughly seven of ten recur within five years, so surveillance cystoscopy begins about three months after resection and continues for years.
steps.say: Non muscle invasive cancers recur often but progress less, so regular cystoscopy surveillance catches them early.

steps.tx: Cancer growing into the bladder muscle layer is **muscle invasive bladder cancer**. It can spread to nodes and distant organs, so radical treatment is needed. Chemotherapy before surgery improves survival in suitable patients. Cisplatin based chemotherapy before surgery gives a modest but real survival gain, so fitness for cisplatin is assessed early.
steps.say: Muscle invasive bladder cancer can spread widely, so radical treatment with chemotherapy is needed.
